subject: Capacity sizing inputs & procurement lead times for ACME deal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@nova-oem.com>, capacity@cloudx.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01 09:12 -0800
Subject: Capacity sizing inputs & procurement lead times for ACME deal

Thomas / Priya / CloudX team —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As we finalize the MAP and the Dedicated capacity commit for ACME, we need firm procurement lead times and any bridge options. Quick summary / asks: 

- Target go-live: 2027-01-18 (ACME exec requested first tenant live).
- Requested dedicated footprint (initial): 16x H100-equivalent GPUs (single-tenant pool), expected average concurrency profile attached in ACME-MAP.
- Key asks for each vendor: 
  * OEM (Nova): confirmed ship ETA for reserved racks / estimated build/provisioning calendar (weeks).
  * Cloud provider (CloudX): earliest reservation window and guaranteed capacity dates for a 16-GPU dedicated reserved pool; any ability to accelerate for deal-driven commitment.
  * Alternatives: options for temporary shared burst capacity, credits if hardware slips, and short-term CPU-backed proxy for dev/QA.

Please reply with concrete lead times, major milestone dates, and any pre-requisite POs or deposit amounts that will accelerate fulfillment. Attaching our proposed capacity MAP for reference.

Next step: I'll collate responses and propose a contingency (bridge) plan to present to ACME by 2026-11-22.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ACME-MAP-proposed-capacity.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)]
From: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@nova-oem.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03 11:04 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sizing inputs & procurement lead times for ACME deal

Marissa / Thomas —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick responses below: 

- OEM lead time: 12–14 weeks from PO receipt for the standard H100 chassis build + on-site integration, assuming no custom ASIC requests. If we receive a 30% deposit within 7 business days, we can prioritize along the next production slot and reduce to ~9 weeks.
- Shipping & staging: 5 business days onsite for racking & burn-in once chassis arrive; remote provisioning can begin earlier for firmware staging.
- Optional services: 1) Factory-validated NVLink config (adds ~1 week); 2) Onsite engineer for first-week handoff (recommended).
- Quote attached: Nova preliminary quote includes unit pricing, optional onsite labor line items, and lead-time-dependent escalation fees.

Caveats: current component constraints (PCIE switches) may cause +/- 2 week variance if PO is delayed past 2026-11-15. If Redwood/ACME needs earlier availability, we can prioritize an allocation but it requires an allocation fee and a signed MOU.

Attaching: nova-quote-20261101.pdf

Regards,
Priya Sinha
Enterprise Accounts — Nova OEM
[Attachment: nova-quote-20261101.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)]
From: CloudX Capacity <capacity@cloudx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05 15:28 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sizing inputs & procurement lead times for ACME deal

Marissa —

We can support a reserved dedicated pool for ACME in us-west-2 with the following windows: 

- Standard reservation lead time: 4–6 weeks after contract signature and payment profile confirmed.
- Accelerated reservation: If Redwood provides proof of deal (HubSpot deal id) and a purchase guarantee, we can commit to a 2-week provisioning window in a limited early-allocation pool (subject to a capacity acceleration surcharge).
- Preemptible burst: We can offer burst capacity (spot-equivalent) for dev/test immediately upon contract signature, but it is not suitable for production SLA.
- SLA & credits: For reserved pools we provide 99.9% uptime SLA; for acceleration requests we can add a service-level credit schedule in the term sheet.

We have attached the reserve term sheet for review. Please note our ability to accelerate depends on other committed customers in the region; we recommend executing any MOU for allocation by 2026-11-12 to lock the accelerated slot.

Best,
CloudX Capacity Desk
[Attachment: cloudx-reserve-term-sheet.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)]
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@nova-oem.com>
Date: 2026-11-11 09:03 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sizing inputs & procurement lead times for ACME deal

Looping in infra notes —

- Sizing confirmation: Based on ACME's expected token throughput and 99th-percentile latency goals, initial 16x H100-equivalent is reasonable for week-1 production but we should plan horizontal scale to 24 GPUs within 8 weeks of go-live.
- Bridge options: 
  * Option A (fastest): CloudX accelerated reservation for production footprint (2-week provisioning) + OEM long-term delivery for Nov/Dec ground truth.
  * Option B (cost-balanced): OEM delivery for primary capacity + CloudX spot burst for QA/dev until on-prem racks are live.
  * Option C (contingency): Shared Redwood Dedicated pool (multi-tenant) configured with guaranteed QoS lanes; requires a short addendum to our Dedicated contract.
- Risk mitigations: Add delivery SLAs into the OEM PO with milestone-based credits; require CloudX to commit an accelerated slot by 2026-11-12 or Redwood will need to buy an interim reserve.

I'll prepare an engineering timeline matrix (week-by-week actions) once we lock the chosen bridge option.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Thomas Reed <thomas.reed@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@nova-oem.com>, capacity@cloudx.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20 15:45 -08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity sizing inputs & procurement lead times for ACME deal

Thanks everyone — consolidating decisions and next steps below (for ACME exec review on Monday):

Decisions: 
- Primary path: Accept Nova OEM quote and issue PO with 30% deposit by 2026-11-22 to target a 9-week OEM lead time and stay on schedule for a 2027-01-18 soft launch.
- Bridge: Execute CloudX accelerated reservation for the 16-GPU production pool; CloudX to confirm accelerated slot by 2026-11-12 (they are tracking; Marissa to provide HubSpot proof-of-deal).
- Contingency: If OEM slips more than 2 weeks, Redwood will stand up a temporary single-tenant lane in our shared Dedicated pool to preserve SLA for ACME; ACME will be notified and credited per contract.

Action items (owners & dates):
- ACME (Thomas): Confirm acceptance of bridge approach and approve deposit timeline — due 2026-11-21.
- Marissa: Upload HubSpot proof-of-deal to CloudX & sign MOU for accelerated slot — due 2026-11-12 (in progress).
- Dev: Produce week-by-week provisioning matrix and cutover checklist — due 2026-11-24.
- Marcus: Coordinate Nova PO terms for delivery credits and optional onsite engineer line item — due 2026-11-22.
- Hannah: Draft contract addendum for temporary single-tenant lane (if needed) and credit schedule — due 2026-11-23.

I'll prepare a brief one-page ASR (Ask / Status / Risks) for the Monday review and include the attached quotes/term sheet. If any vendor can't meet the dates above, flag immediately.

Thanks all —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: nova-quote-20261101.pdf, ACME-MAP-proposed-capacity.xlsx, cloudx-reserve-term-sheet.pdf]
